records.question: By what percentage did coral cover at the Taulaga transects decrease following the February 1987 storm?
ground_truth_chunks: During February 1987, Swains Island was struck by a severe storm. High waves damaged a major part of the shoreline and decimated the village of Taulaga on the south-west side of the island (Itano, 1987).
Coral cover recorded prior to the storm at the Taulaga transects on the SW side of the island, (see Itano, 1987), had decreased by 93-100%.

records.question: In what water depth were the transects laid?
records.ground_truth_answer: They were laid "in 1 Om of water."
ground_truth_chunks: Five 50m transects were laid consecutively on the reef front in 1 Om of water, at each of two sites on the south-west facing side of Swains Island (Fig. 1).

records.question: Was there a significant change in mean percent total live coral cover between 1996 and 1998 surveys?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — there was no significant change in mean percent total live coral cover between 1996 and 1998 surveys (p = 0.563).
ground_truth_chunks: A visual survey of the reef front from 3 -25m on the south-west side of Swains Island opposite the village of Taulaga (Fig. I), detected no obvious physical damage to the reef or live corals. Accordingly, there was no significant change in mean percent total live coral cover (mean + s.e.) between 1996 and 1998 surveys (p= 0.563) or among sites within surveys **0,** = 0.02).

The mean total percent coral cover at SW1 was slightly greater in 1996 (63.7 k1.6) than in 1998 (56.2 + 1.5). Conversely, total coral cover at SW2 was lower in 1996 (44.5 + 4.5) than in 1998 (57.2 + 3.9, refer Fig. 2. These differences are most likely to be attributed to natural variation in coral density and location of survey transects.

records.question: Was there a significant change in total coral cover between 1996 and 1998 on the reef front south of Taulaga?
records.ground_truth_answer: No. There was no significant change in total coral cover between 1996 and 1998 on the reef front south of Taulaga.
ground_truth_chunks: Heavy south-west swells generated by hurricane Ron as it passed to the north of Swains Island in March 1998 had no visible impact on the coral reef.
There was no significant change in total coral cover between 1996 and 1998 on the reef front south of Taulaga.
